title: Photographs for description: harbour at dawn, railway station at night
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 8 (Photographs for description: harbour at dawn, railway station at night (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 8: Description: planning from a prompt or image with the CLOSER lens. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: What Section C asks
points: One piece from a choice of three

head: Step
Job
rows: two or three senses, not five lists

parts.text: C: grey light, still water, gulls asleep on posts
L: water, then the moored boats, then one rope
O: a frayed rope creaking against a post
S: diesel smell, cold rail, a single gull's cry
E and R: the sun breaks through; the same water now gold

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A six-line plan with one dominant impression: stillness before work begins.

keywords.def: where the describer stands and what they can notice
the single feeling the whole description builds
to do with sight, sound, smell, touch or taste

questions.q: Write a CLOSER plan for: 'Describe a railway station late at night.'
questions.a: Six short lines, one dominant impression (e.g. loneliness), wide to close.

questions.q: Choose a dominant impression for your plan and give two details that build it.
questions.a: For example: loneliness: one figure-free bench, an echo of footsteps.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write the opening paragraph of your station description (C and L only). Starter: 'At this hour, the station...'
questions.a: A controlled opening: place, time, wide view, then a lead into one area, with one dominant mood.

questions.q: Extend: add one sentence that zooms to a significant object (O).
questions.a: For example: Above the bench, the clock's second hand jerks forward as if it, too, were tired.

questions.q: Stretch: rewrite your first sentence to be shorter and sharper.
Which plan risks losing AO4 marks for a description?
options: One object that carries the mood
A long story about a fisherman's whole day
Wide view, close-up, the light changing
questions.a: B) A long story about a fisherman's whole day. Description should stay in one place and moment; a plot drifts off task.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: what would you notice first, and why?
questions.a: Answers vary; the first detail should set the dominant impression.
